citations.excerpt: Software engineering is the art and science of building software...
Code is written! Programming is crucial to SE. But SE is more than programming.
How do you build something with no physical size, that you can't see or feel? ... know what to build, when even your customer doesn't? ... co-ordinate a team of people to do this, on a large scale?

recall.a: Coding plus team coordination, requirements, design, implementation, testing, verification and maintenance.
recall.q: Without looking: SE is more than programming — name the other activities.

sections.heading: Introduction
paras: Software engineering (SE) is the art and science of building software — not just writing code, but doing so deliberately, reliably, and at team scale. The unit opens with a blunt claim: SE centres around coding, yet coding can go badly wrong without everything around it.

Why does that matter for your midterm? Because nearly every planning question is really asking: can you show the engineering around the code — the plans, estimates, graphs and trade-offs that keep a project honest?

sections.heading: Core explanation
paras: Programming is crucial to SE, but SE is more than programming. The lecture lists what the rest looks like: co-ordinating a team and managing the project, understanding user requirements, designing components, implementing them, testing piece by piece, verifying the software meets its goals, and maintaining it afterwards.

Whole books have been written about each of these, and every company does them differently — there is no one-size-fits-all approach. That sentence is worth remembering: examiners reward answers that adapt a technique to the situation rather than reciting one true method.

bullets: It has no physical size — you cannot see or feel it, so progress is invisible without explicit models (graphs, backlogs, charts).
Customers often do not know what they want, so requirements must be elicited, not just collected.
Failures hide: you need to know when something goes wrong and how to fix it without breaking the rest.
Coordination overhead grows with team size; communication is part of the product.
Time estimation is structurally uncertain — which is why this unit spends so much time on estimation techniques.
sections.heading: Why software is hard to build
paras: The lecture's challenge slide frames all of this as open questions, and the course answers each one with a concrete tool: WBS answers what to build, planning poker answers how long, activity graphs answer in what order, burn-up charts answer are we on track.

callout.text: Definitions of SE and 'why is SE more than programming' appear as short-answer warm-ups. Answer with the activity list plus one consequence (cost overrun, lawsuit, lost data) to show you grasp the stakes, not just the vocabulary.

sections.heading: Exam relevance
paras: Short-answer questions love this topic because it is easy to mark: list the activities, explain one challenge, connect it to a technique from later in the unit.

summary: Software engineering is the disciplined art of building software at team scale: coding plus planning, requirements, design, testing, verification and maintenance.
title: Software engineering: more than programming
